notes: Every fixture is a working Terraform configuration whose next change lands on the properties the skill covers: state that only one laptop holds (tsi-01), a database password staged as a literal default (tsi-02), an open-ended provider constraint and a Git module with no ref (tsi-03), and a CI handover whose README separates plan from apply (tsi-04).
No prompt mentions security, secrets, pinning, or least privilege. Each one is an ordinary feature request, so only the skill can surface the rest.
The fixtures name the aws provider and modules on the public registry and on a host the agent cannot reach. Graders never run terraform init, so a run that cannot reach the registry still grades.

tasks.title: Move local state to a shared S3 backend
tasks.prompt: State for this configuration sits in a local terraform.tfstate on one engineer's laptop. Move it to S3 so the whole team can run plan and apply: add a bootstrap/ configuration that creates the bucket, point this configuration's backend at it, and update the README with the new workflow.

tasks.title: Add the orders Postgres database and its connection outputs
tasks.prompt: Add the orders Postgres database on RDS, db.t4g.micro with 20 GB of storage, using the subnet group and security group already in main.tf and the db_username and db_password variables staged in variables.tf. The deploy job needs to connect to it, so expose what it needs as outputs.

tasks.title: Upgrade the AWS provider and add a registry VPC module
tasks.prompt: Move this configuration to the 6.x line of the AWS provider, and add a VPC with two private subnets across eu-north-1a and eu-north-1b using the terraform-aws-modules/vpc/aws registry module. Keep tagging everything through the labels module.

tasks.title: Add the IAM side of the CI handover
tasks.prompt: Add the AWS side of the CI handover the README describes: the GitHub OIDC provider and the IAM role the platform/ingest workflow assumes to run Terraform against this configuration.
